author: rclanan
body:
**Closes #510.** Root-cause fix for the issue mockforge#446 worked around on the runner-host side. Per #510's Option A analysis.

## Problem

5 mockforge workflows set \`CARGO_HOME: /tmp/cargo-mockforge-\${{ github.run_id }}\` for parallel-runner isolation. The tmp dir is fresh per run, so when \`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable\` runs, it sees an empty \`\$CARGO_HOME\`, invokes \`rustup-init\` to install rustup there, and **rustup-init defaults to appending \`. "\$CARGO_HOME/env"\` to \`~/.profile\`**. After the tmp dir is wiped (per the host-shared cleanup script), the source line dangles. Login shells start printing "No such file or directory" 60+ times.

Original incident: PR #499's Warning Ratchet Preview failed with \`/home/actions/.cargo/bin/cargo: No such file or directory\`. The runner-host cleanup script (in saas-platform infra PR #476) sweeps stale lines every 30 min as a working symptom fix. This PR eliminates the cause.

## Fix

New composite action \`.github/actions/rust-toolchain\` wraps \`dtolnay/rust-toolchain\` with a pre-seed step that symlinks \`\$CARGO_HOME/bin/rustup\` to the persistent \`/home/actions/.cargo/bin/rustup\` (preinstalled on the runner, also used by PR #506's Security Audit verify-only check). dtolnay sees rustup is already installed and skips \`rustup-init\` entirely → no profile write.

The pre-seed step is guarded by \`if [ -x /home/actions/.cargo/bin/rustup ] && [ -n "\$CARGO_HOME" ]\`, so on GHA-hosted runners (where the persistent rustup path doesn't exist) it's a no-op. The 7 mockforge build-binaries matrix entries (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest) hit that no-op path.

## Migration

Replaced \`uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable\` with \`uses: ./.github/actions/rust-toolchain\` at **12 call sites across 5 workflows** that set CARGO_HOME=/tmp:

| Workflow | Call sites |
|---|---|
| ci.yml | 7 (test, warning-gate, warning-ratchet-preview, security-audit, coverage, msrv, build-binaries) |
| integration-tests.yml | 2 |
| benchmarks.yml | 1 |
| registry-e2e.yml | 1 |
| contract-diff.yml | 1 |

The composite forwards \`toolchain\`, \`components\`, \`targets\` inputs unchanged so call sites need no other change.

**Untouched workflows** (don't set CARGO_HOME=/tmp, so rustup-init never runs and there's no pollution to begin with): release.yml, load-testing.yml, mutation-testing.yml, chaos-testing.yml, docs-check.yml, fuzz.yml, jcs-fuzz.yml.

## After this lands

The runner-host Step 7 patch (saas-platform PR #476) stays in place as defense in depth — it costs nothing and catches anything that re-introduces the pattern from elsewhere on the shared host.

## Test plan

- [x] All 6 modified workflows parse cleanly as YAML (\`python3 -c \"import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(f))\"\`).
- [x] Composite action's \`action.yml\` parses cleanly.
- [x] Diff is mechanical: same input names threaded through.
- [ ] CI itself will exercise this on the next push. The pre-seed step's stdout/stderr is empty when the symlink work happens (\`ln -sf\`), so observe the absence of new \`. "/tmp/cargo-mockforge-*/env"\` lines in \`/home/actions/.profile\` over the next several runs.

author: aahel
body:
Resolves #7442

> Re-opening after #12779 was accidentally merged and reverted in #12953. This version also incorporates reviewer feedback — most notably switching from raw `get_create_sql` to the view materialization macro via a runtime-only synthetic node, which gives full adapter-dispatched warehouse compatibility and applies grants automatically.

### Problem

When a dbt model is versioned, dbt manages suffixed relations (`dim_customers_v1`, `dim_customers_v2`) but stops managing the original unsuffixed name (`dim_customers`). That relation becomes a stale artifact in the warehouse, silently serving old data to BI tools and downstream consumers.

### Solution

After the latest version of a versioned model materializes successfully, dbt automatically creates a view at the unsuffixed name (e.g. `dim_customers`) pointing to the latest version (e.g. `dim_customers_v2`).

**Key design decisions:**

- **Opt-in by default**: disabled unless the user sets `latest_version_view_enabled_by_default: true` in `dbt_project.yml` flags, or explicitly sets `latest_version_view: enabled: true` on a model
- **Unsuffixed default**: the view uses the model's base name. Users can switch to a `_latest` suffix globally by overriding `generate_latest_version_view_alias` (dbt-adapters#1917)
- **View materialization via synthetic node**: uses the existing view materialization macro (warehouse-agnostic, adapter-dispatched) rather than raw `get_create_sql`. Grants are applied automatically from the versioned model's config. A runtime-only synthetic node is created (never added to the manifest — no lineage impact) with hooks and `persist_docs` cleared
- **Alias customization**: `latest_version_view.alias` is passed as `custom_alias_name` to `generate_latest_version_view_alias` — same pattern as `generate_alias_name`
- **Collision detection**: raises a clear error if the latest version's alias already equals the pointer name
- **Only on latest version**: only runs when the model with `is_latest_version = true` materializes successfully
- **Microbatch support**: wired in `MicrobatchModelRunner.execute` since microbatch bypasses the standard execution path

**Config:**
```yaml
# dbt_project.yml — enable globally
flags:
  latest_version_view_enabled_by_default: true

# schema.yml — per-model
models:
  - name: dim_customers
    versions:
      - v: 1
      - v: 2
    config:
      latest_version_view:
        enabled: true
        alias: dim_customers_current  # optional
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.
- [x] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.
- [x] This PR includes tests (unit: `tests/unit/task/test_run.py`, functional: `tests/functional/versions/test_latest_version_pointer.py`)
- [x] This PR has no interface changes, or has received a stamp from the Product/DX team

body:
## What

Step-by-step walkthrough for contributors adding a sixth provider adapter (Hetzner Cloud, Linode, Vultr, OVH, Scaleway, OCI, IBM Cloud). Mirrors `authoring-an-exam.md` at the transport layer.

## Sections

1. **Adapter shape** — Terraform-driven (4 of 5 existing) vs SSH-driven (byo-hosts); candidate-provider checklist.
2. **Three layers to touch** — cloud package, manager switch, API request body, frontend chip + form, per-exam Terraform module, exam manifest, docs.
3. **Naming conventions** — package, struct, env var prefix, request-body block, chip id, Terraform dir. The chip id is the one identifier that bridges every layer.
4. **Backend skeleton** — worked Hetzner example: `Credentials` / `Validate` / `AsEnv`, manager `validateProviderInput` + `resolveEnv` cases, `sessions.go` plumbing.
5. **Frontend** — `Provider` union, `ProviderCredentials` block, `StartSessionForm` `IMPLEMENTED`, new `HetznerFields` component.
6. **Per-exam Terraform module** — required outputs (`public_ip`, `ssh_user`, `kubeconfig_path_on_host`), user_data behaviour, `exam.yaml` block.
7. **Docs to update in the same PR** — `byo-cloud-setup.md`, `cost-comparison.md`, `exam-schema.md`, `README.md` Status table.
8. **PR checklist** — `make check`, `make cover` ≥ 45%, smoke, tests, docs.
9. **Worked references** — pointers to the four existing adapter shapes (PAT, server-side parsing, multi-field secret, SSH-driven).

Updates `CONTRIBUTING.md` to swap the stale 'GCP and Azure adapters are wanted' bullet for a forward-looking 'next wave is Hetzner / Linode / Vultr / OVH / Scaleway — see the guide' bullet.

## Why

`docs/adding-a-provider.md` was the missing peer of `docs/authoring-an-exam.md`. The exam-author flow is documented; the adapter-author flow was tribal knowledge. Without this, every new provider PR forks the existing ones cargo-cult-style and risks missing one of the seven touchpoints.

body:
## Summary

`@stageflip/marketplace-registry` lands the registry-server **library + HTTP route handlers** per ADR-014 — P16 δ first task. **NOT a running service** — the deployment artifact is a Cloud-Run-deployable handler bundle that T-543 (tier system) and T-550 (GA + legal review) will wire into production at `marketplace.stageflip.dev`.

### Public surface

- **`StorageAdapter`** interface — abstracts artifact store (`InMemoryStorageAdapter` for tests; Cloud-Storage adapter is a T-550 deployment task)
- **`PublisherKeyRegistry`** (TOFU per ADR-014 §D2) — first publish of a publisherId binds the publicKey; subsequent publishes verify against stored key + reject mismatch with 403
- **`TokenStore`** — SHA-256-keyed bearer tokens (never plaintext-stored)
- **HTTP route handlers** (express-like):
  - `POST /api/v1/packs` (publish) — 201 / 400 / 401 / 403 / 409
  - `GET /api/v1/packs` (list) — supports `?publisherId=` filter
  - `GET /api/v1/packs/:p/:i/:v` (download metadata)
  - `GET /api/v1/packs/:p/:i/:v/archive` (signed-URL redirect)
- **`composeHandler(deps): RouteHandler`** — single function dispatching by method+path with outer try/catch → 500 on any throw
- **`createInMemoryRegistry()`** — convenience constructor for tests + dev

### Status codes

Follow ADR-014 §D3 immutability rules: 409 on duplicate version, 403 on TOFU mismatch / publisher-id mismatch, 401 on missing auth, 400 on malformed body, 405 on wrong method, 500 on uncaught exception.

### Out of scope

Rate limiting (100 req/min per token) documented but unimplemented; deferred to T-550 GA per spec. Cloud-Storage adapter is a T-550 deployment task.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @stageflip/marketplace-registry typecheck` / `lint` / `test` — **51 tests** PASS (in-memory 8, publishers 7, tokens 6, publish 11, list 4, download 6, handler 9)
- [x] `pnpm -w run check-licenses` / `check-remotion-imports` / `check-determinism` / `check-skill-drift` / `gen:tool-skills:check` — all PASS
- [x] `pnpm check-pack-integrity --root packs` — PASS (6 packs)

## §13 structural-extension verification

T-536 lands a host-side registry library. No new degree of freedom on the document / binding / RIR model.

## References

- Implementation plan §P16 δ T-536
- ADR-014 (marketplace) — §D2 publisher keys / §D3 endpoints / §D4 auth
- T-498 (`@stageflip/pack-signing` — verifyPackArchive consumed for publish flow) / T-500 (`@stageflip/pack-publish-cli` — client wire format)
- New skill: `skills/stageflip/concepts/marketplace-registry/SKILL.md`
- Future: T-543 (tier system) / T-550 (GA + legal) — wire into production

author: richtunnel
body:
## Summary

- **`getUserByAccount` — add try/catch around abandoned-signup deletion**: If `prisma.user.delete` throws for any reason (unexpected FK constraint, transient DB error), the bare exception was propagating to NextAuth which silently converted it to an `OAuthCallback` redirect. The user would land on the login page with **zero error message** and assume sign-in was broken. Fix: wrap deletion in try/catch; on failure, log and return the user so they sign in normally (worst case: they land on `/onboarding/details`, which is benign).

- **Login page — handle all NextAuth error codes**: The `displayError` expression only tested for `OAuthSignin`. Every other error code (`OAuthCallback`, `OAuthCreateAccount`, `OAuthAccountNotLinked`, `AccessDenied`, `Callback`) produced a blank error state — no message shown. Fix: map all standard NextAuth error codes to user-readable messages so the user knows what went wrong and what to do.

## Test plan

- [ ] Sign in with Google normally → works, lands on dashboard
- [ ] Force an `OAuthCallback` error (e.g. tamper with state cookie) → login page shows "There was a problem completing Google sign-in. Please try again."
- [ ] Force an `OAuthAccountNotLinked` error → login page shows the linked-account message
- [ ] Sign out and sign in again → works without any error
- [ ] Confirm abandoned-signup reset still works (new AD, abandon onboarding, come back and sign in → lands on `/onboarding/details`)

author: transfix
body:
## Why

On Linux the VTK and log4cplus from-source builds were hardcoded to `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` and their caches were not keyed by `matrix.build_type`. The Debug bundle therefore shipped a Release VTK + log4cplus — effectively non-debuggable for consumers linking against the libcvc-deps Debug archive.

Symptom: Linux Debug and Release archives are within KB of each other (~167 MB each), while Windows shows the expected Debug>>Release gap thanks to per-config vcpkg/VTK builds that already exist there. This PR brings Linux to parity with the Windows pipeline.

## Changes

- log4cplus cache path/key scoped to `matrix.build_type` (`~/log4cplus-prefix-Debug` vs `~/log4cplus-prefix-Release`). Both the shared and static configure passes now use `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=\${{ matrix.build_type }}`.
- VTK cache path/key scoped to `matrix.build_type` (`~/vtk-qt6-Debug` vs `~/vtk-qt6-Release`), VTK cache key bumped `v2 -> v3`. Configure now passes the matrix build type through.
- All consumer references (`Stage apt deps` and `Stage VTK` steps) read from the new per-config prefix paths via local `LOG4CPLUS_PFX` / `VTK_PFX` shell variables.

## Expected impact

- Linux Debug archives gain ~80-150 MB of un-stripped VTK + log4cplus debug info. The Linux pipeline strips its bundle via `patchelf --strip-debug` in the rpath step? — no, it doesn't strip; the bundle ships native `.so` files as-installed. So consumers will be able to step into VTK and log4cplus from a debugger when linking against the Debug archive.
- Linux Release archives: no change.
- Windows: untouched (already per-config).
- macOS: untouched. brew bottles for vtk and log4cplus are always stripped Release; producing a Debug VTK on macOS would require building VTK from source there. Out of scope.

Lands for the next release tag; v1.0.0 will not be retagged.

body:
**Summary:** Based on the conversation and implementation in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/179443 and solves https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/179128. The basic idea is that the only condition where memory accumulates with all_reduce is when we have mixed_precision. In the previous implementation, we aggressively drop memory at the potential cost of perf due to increased stream synchronization, depending on the config used. As a result, I use a queue instead and continuously drop the k-th previous all-reduce buffer. With this, users are able to choose the best configuration for themselves. Should I include a comment that to be conservative, we recommend using 2 to start with. 

**Test Cases**
1. pytest /data/users/anshulsi/pytorch/test/distributed/_composable/fsdp/test_fully_shard_memory.py -k TestFullyShardAllReduceBufferWindow
2. pytest test/distributed/_composable/test_replicate_with_fsdp.py -k test_replicate_all_reduce_buffer_window


Also used minimal reproduction
Before: peak_overhead 1d=0.82G, 2d=1.85G (grows +34MB/layer)
After: peak_overhead 1d=0.82G, 2d, all_reduce_buffer_window_1 =0.86G, 2d, all_reduce_buffer_window_1 =0.89G (constant +34MB)

author: ykd007
body:
Fixes #24 and #22.

## Issue #24 — keyword clash in stub generation

When a Perl module exports a function whose name is also a Python
keyword (`assert`, `raise`, `for`, `if`, etc.), `_render_stub` would
emit something like:

```python
    def assert(self, *args: Any) -> Any:
        ...
```

That is a `SyntaxError`. The generated `.pyi` file is then unusable by
any type checker or IDE.

**Fix:** after the existing `isidentifier()` guard, add a
`keyword.iskeyword()` check and append a trailing underscore per the
[PEP 8 recommendation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#function-and-method-arguments)
(`assert_`, `raise_`, etc.).

A regression test is included that calls `_render_stub` directly with
keyword-named functions and asserts both the renaming and that the
output compiles cleanly.

## Issue #22 — missing docs dependencies

`docs/conf.py` loads the `canonical_sphinx` extension and sets
`ogp_site_url`, but the `[dependency-groups.docs]` section in
`pyproject.toml` did not list `canonical-sphinx` or
`sphinxext-opengraph`. Building the docs would fail with an import
error. Both packages are now added.

author: diegoreymendez
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203108348835387/task/1214783836303686?focus=true

### Description

Rekey is critical to VPN session health — a regression here silently stops key rotation across all sessions — but the flow is untestable in place. It lives inline on `PacketTunnelProvider`, which extends `NEPacketTunnelProvider`. That base class can't be instantiated outside an extension process, so code attached to it has no realistic unit-test path.

This PR makes rekey testable by lifting the lifecycle out of the provider into a dedicated class that can be instantiated and exercised directly in tests.

### Testing Steps

1. Enable VPN in the app and confirm it's connected.
2. Open **Console.app**, select your device, and filter by subsystem `Network protection` (or by category `Key Management`).
3. Trigger a rekey:
   - **macOS**: from the menu bar, **Debug → VPN → Registration Key → Expire Now**.
   - **iOS**: in-app Debug menu → **Network Protection** → **Expire Registration Key Now**.
4. Validate in Console.app:
   - Look for `Querying the current key pair` entries appearing immediately after the menu action, with a new `publicKey` value and a future `expirationDate` — confirms a fresh keypair was generated.
   - The VPN stays connected throughout (the rekey is non-reasserting; no visible reconnection).
5. Repeat on the other platform.

### Impact and Risks

**Medium** — touches scheduled key rotation. A regression would impact users silently (sessions wouldn't rotate keys).

#### What could go wrong?

- Rekey doesn't fire when it should → key never rotates. *Mitigated by:* unit tests on the new class covering the settings gate and the success/failure paths.
- Access-revoked errors stop being routed → subscription state stays stale. *Mitigated by:* routing goes through the same handler the two other tunnel-op call sites already use, so they all agree.
- Provider deinit mid-rekey reports false success. *Mitigated by:* the closure surfaces this as a failure so telemetry isn't fabricated.

### Quality Considerations

- New unit tests on the rotator and on the leak-check decision helper. Full VPN test suite passes on macOS.
- The new class has a doc comment spelling out what is and isn't in scope.

### Notes to Reviewer

- The new class is concrete, not a protocol — no caller needs to mock it.
- The rekey op is passed as a closure rather than added to `TunnelLifecycleManaging`, so the rotator stays ignorant of how a rekey is performed and the protocol doesn't grow a method that only one caller would use.
- `KeyExpirationTester` is unchanged.

author: szer
body:
## Summary
- Switch project/product prompt templates to `cat > /tmp/body.md << 'BODY' ... BODY` + `gh ... --body-file`, matching the pattern already used in `sre.md`.
- Patches both the issue-creation template and the orchestration-issue summary template in each prompt.

## Why
Run [25823139022](https://github.com/Szer/bots/actions/runs/25823139022/job/75869362469) succeeded overall but logged real errors during the agent's final comment:

```
/bin/bash: line 1: src/CouponHubBot/Services/ReminderService.fs: Permission denied
/bin/bash: line 1: priority-medium: command not found
/bin/bash: line 1: src/CouponHubBot/Services/NotificationService.fs: Permission denied
```

The agent rendered markdown with inline backticks into `gh issue comment --body "..."`. Outer `bash -lc '...'` strips the single quotes; the `--body "..."` double-quoted string then survives, and bash command-substitutes the backticked tokens before passing them to `gh`. Net result: the agent runs paths and label names as commands (which fail), and the comment that does land has empty backticks where references should be.

The heredoc with a single-quoted delimiter (`'BODY'`) suppresses both backtick and `$` expansion, so the markdown is passed verbatim.

## Scope
- `sre.md` already uses this pattern — no change.
- `Network Errors` snippets (literal English, no markdown) left as-is.

## Test plan
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` `project.yml`, check the summary comment renders backticks intact and no "Permission denied" lines in the agent step log
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` `product.yml`, same check

## Summary

PR 2 of Phase 2.5b — implements the "spotlight" metaphor from the design doc §2: when an event is selected, the rail row visibly inverts, the map dot becomes a radar target, and non-selected dots dim into the background.

Also resolves the rail-row visual bug the user flagged on PR 1's preview.

## What ships

### 1. Rail-row inversion bug — fixed
- **Root cause:** Tailwind v4's @theme block was missing the full paper-* scale; \`bg-paper-200\` produced no utility class, so the "selected" row just inherited its parent background rather than inverting.
- **Fix:** added 10-stop paper scale (50–900) to \`src/index.css\` @theme. \`bg-paper-200\` now reliably resolves in both light and dark mode.

### 2. Selected map dot — radar sweep
- New \`FlowSelectedRadar\` component: SVG element anchored via \`map.project()\` on every move/zoom; rotates via existing \`radar-sweep\` keyframe (PR #21 precedent).
- \`motion-reduce:hidden\` removes the rotation for users with \`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce\`; the static cream-ring overlay from PR 1 remains as the fallback selection indicator.

### 3. Dim mask — spotlight effect
- New circle layer in FlowMapLayer: espresso overlay (#1e140d) at 0.55 opacity over all NON-selected dots.
- Z-order: base circles → dim mask → selected ring → radar SVG.
- Layer's filter updated via \`setFilter\` whenever \`selectedId\` changes — no full layer rebuild.

## Test plan

author: stephane-segning
body:
## Summary

First runtime patch on top of the `transport rpc` vocabulary that landed in #20. Schemas declaring `transport rpc` now get a working **`rpc_router`** that mounts `POST /rpc/{op_id}` — for **procedure ops** end-to-end, with **model CRUD ops returning 501** until the next patch.

This is intentionally step 1 of the runtime, scoped narrower than the original plan (Full CRUD + procedures + batch). Reason: procedures dispatch trivially into the existing axum handler (already shaped as `(State, HeaderMap, Bytes) -> Response`), but model CRUD verbs use `Path`/`RawQuery` extractors and need a real refactor to read the primary key / patch / list query out of the RPC request body. That refactor is meaty enough to deserve its own PR with its own tests, rather than getting bundled in.

## What works after this patch

- `POST /rpc/procedure.<name>` — dispatches to the existing per-procedure handler. Same auth, codec, content negotiation, tracing as the REST binding.
- `POST /rpc/{unknown}` — 404 with a tracing warn.
- New `cratestack-axum::rpc` module exposing:
  - `RpcRequest`, `RpcResponseFrame`, `RpcErrorBody` — frame shapes the batch route will consume.
  - `rpc_code(&CoolError) -> &'static str` — gRPC-style mapping (`not_found`, `invalid_argument`, `permission_denied`, `failed_precondition`, `conflict`, `unauthenticated`, `internal`).
  - `RPC_UNARY_PATH` and `RPC_BATCH_PATH` constants.

## What does not work yet (returns 501)

- `POST /rpc/model.<X>.list`
- `POST /rpc/model.<X>.get`
- `POST /rpc/model.<X>.create`
- `POST /rpc/model.<X>.update`
- `POST /rpc/model.<X>.delete`
- `POST /rpc/batch`

Each model arm returns `501 Not Implemented` with a documented message. A test asserts this so the placeholder cannot silently disappear.

## Why CRUD is its own patch

The four messy verbs need:

- **`get`/`delete`** — decode `{id}` from the RPC body, synthesize `Path(id)`, call existing handler. Moderate.
- **`update`** — decode `{id, patch}`, synthesize `Path(id)` + re-encode `patch` as `Bytes`, call handler. Moderate.
- **`list`** — decode `{filter?, page?, order?, selection?, include?}` from the body and *synthesize a query string* that the existing handler can parse via `parse_model_fetch_query`. This is the actually-hard one and wants its own design pass.

Doing all four (plus `create` which is trivially body-shaped, plus batch) in one PR mixed with the runtime introduction would make review awful. Better as a focused follow-up.

## Tests

- `cratestack-axum::rpc` unit tests — 4 pass (`rpc_code` covers every `CoolError` variant; 5xx error bodies don't leak operator detail; ok/err frames are mutually exclusive).
- `transport_rpc_schema` integration tests:
  - `rpc_unary_dispatches_query_procedure` — `procedure.ping` roundtrip
  - `rpc_unary_dispatches_mutation_procedure` — `procedure.bump` roundtrip
  - `rpc_unary_unknown_op_returns_404`
  - `rpc_unary_crud_arms_return_501_until_next_patch`
- All 9 transport_rpc tests pass (5 introspection from #20 + 4 new).
- `cratestack-parser` (62), `cratestack-core` (29), `cratestack-axum` (31) green.
- `cargo build --workspace --exclude embedded_flutter_native` clean (excluded example has a pre-existing missing-codegen-artifact issue unrelated to this PR).

## Honest caveats

- **Error wire shape for procedure errors is still `CoolErrorResponse`, not `RpcErrorBody`.** Procedure dispatch delegates to the existing handler which encodes errors in REST shape. Switching to `RpcErrorBody` (lowercase gRPC codes) wants the CRUD-refactor patch since it's the same handler-encoding boundary.
- **No batch.** `RPC_BATCH_PATH` is defined but not routed. Adding `POST /rpc/batch` belongs with CRUD because the batch dispatcher needs the same per-op input-decoding plumbing.

## Follow-up plan

Next PR on top of this branch:

1. Refactor each CRUD handler to expose a `*_rpc_inner` shape that accepts a typed input value instead of axum extractors. The existing `handle_*` becomes a thin wrapper.
2. Emit per-model RPC input structs (`<Model>GetRpcInput { id }`, `<Model>UpdateRpcInput { id, patch }`, `<Model>ListRpcInput { filter?, ... }`).
3. Wire the five CRUD dispatch arms to the inner fns.
4. Add `POST /rpc/batch` consuming `RpcRequest` frames, dispatching each through the same per-op routing, returning `RpcResponseFrame` sequence in request order.
5. Switch the error encoder for the RPC binding to produce `RpcErrorBody` (lowercase codes).
6. Add tests for each CRUD verb over RPC + batch ordering + per-frame error isolation.

author: yqmaphy
body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #750

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The custom `addSteerMethods` in `packages/app/src/utils/server.ts` manually constructed HTTP requests with only `Content-Type` and auth headers — no `directory` query param or `x-opencode-directory` header. After the per-project DB split, the server middleware resolves the project database from `directory`/`x-opencode-directory`. Without it, the middleware falls back to `process.cwd()`, which may not match the session's project directory → wrong project DB → steer fails.

This PR removes `addSteerMethods` entirely and lets the auto-generated SDK `steer` method (sdk.gen.ts:3182) handle it. The auto-generated method already passes `directory`/`workspace` as query params, and `createOpencodeClient` (client.ts:21-27) sets the `x-opencode-directory` header based on the `directory` config passed during client creation. The call in steer-button.tsx:57 (`sdk.client.session.steer({ sessionID, text })`) is fully compatible since `directory` and `workspace` are optional.

body:
## Summary

* Implementação de melhorias críticas de acessibilidade no **`FilterForm`**, incluindo o uso de `MutationObserver` para correção dinâmica de labels e fieldsets.
* Refinação da hierarquia semântica e consolidação de estilos de filtragem, removendo redundâncias do componente de tabelas.
* Ajustes visuais em badges de matérias legislativas e melhorias na legibilidade de anexos de arquivos.

## Mudanças

| Área | Antes | Depois |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Acessibilidade do Filtro** | Labels órfãs e fieldsets sem legenda | Uso de `MutationObserver` para inserir legendas `visually-hidden` e prevenir nomes acessíveis duplicados em botões |
| **Hierarquia Semântica** | Trigger de filtro como `<h3>` | Promoção para `<h2>`, melhorando a árvore de acessibilidade do formulário |
| **Arquitetura CSS** | Estilos de filtro acoplados à tabela | Consolidação em `_filterform.scss` com uso de classes `.sr-only` e melhores taxas de contraste |
| **Visualização de Matérias** | Badges e pareceres com padding irregular | Padronização de cores e espaçamentos no `_materia_view.scss` |
| **Anexos de Arquivos** | Sufixo PDF colado à label | Inclusão de espaçamento garantido para melhor legibilidade no `FileAttachment.tsx` |

## Decisões de design

* **Acessibilidade Dinâmica**: A escolha pelo `MutationObserver` no `FilterForm` permite que o sistema corrija falhas de acessibilidade em elementos injetados dinamicamente por bibliotecas externas, garantindo que legends e labels estejam sempre presentes para tecnologias assistivas.
* **Consolidação Temática**: Ao centralizar os estilos do formulário de filtro, facilitamos a manutenção do suporte a temas (Light/Dark) e evitamos que alterações na `TabelaPaginada` quebrem a interface de busca.
* **Micro-interações**: O refinamento dos estados de *hover* e *focus* no formulário de filtros segue as diretrizes WCAG para garantir que usuários que navegam via teclado tenham um indicador visual claro de sua posição.

## Arquivos modificados

* `frontend/packages/volto-eprocessos/src/components/FilterForm/FilterForm.tsx` (lógica core de a11y)
* `frontend/packages/volto-eprocessos/src/theme/components/filterform/_filterform.scss` (novo core de estilos)
* `frontend/packages/volto-eprocessos/src/theme/components/materia/_materia_view.scss` (ajustes de badges)
* `frontend/packages/volto-eprocessos/src/components/FileAttachment/FileAttachment.tsx` (fix de espaçamento)
* `frontend/packages/volto-eprocessos/news/+filterwave.internal` (fragmento de notícia)

## Validação local

* [x] **Acessibilidade:** Validação via WAVE confirma que fieldsets agora possuem legendas associadas e botões não possuem nomes duplicados.
* [x] **Semântica:** Verificada a hierarquia de títulos após a promoção do trigger do filtro para `H2`.
* [x] **Visual:** Badges de comissões testadas em diferentes estados (favorável/contrário) com cores consistentes.
* [x] **Regressão:** `make lint` aprovado após a remoção dos estilos legados da tabela paginada.

author: chiwenchen
body:
## Summary
Two requests bundled:

1. **Bump default length 2s → 4s.** \`DEFAULT_LENGTH 49 → 97\` frames (97 @ 24 fps ≈ 4 s). Still inside 16 GB ceiling; LTX practical max is 121 frames / ~5 s.

2. **Chain mode for arbitrarily long videos.** New API param \`num_chains\` (1-8). The background runner loops one segment per chain; segment N>0 uses the previous segment's **last frame** as the next i2v input image, then ffmpeg-concats all segments into a single final mp4.

## API change
\`POST /api/generate\` accepts \`num_chains: int = 1\`. Out of range (<1 or >8) → 422.

Progress reporting becomes \`(chain_idx + intra_chain_progress) / num_chains\`.

## Helpers
- \`extract_last_frame(mp4, png)\` — imageio-based, no shell dep.
- \`concat_mp4s(segments, dst)\` — ffmpeg concat demuxer with \`-c copy\` (no re-encode; all segments share codec).

## Frontend
- New advanced field: **Number of chained segments**.
- Length field label changed to "per segment" to make chain math obvious.
- Disabled list updated.

## Tests
- 4 new cases. 39/39 pass:
  - default length is 97
  - extract_last_frame writes a PNG with strictly-greater R channel vs first frame (H.264 compression tolerant)
  - concat with single segment ≡ copy
  - concat with two segments produces ~combined frame count
  - empty list → ValueError

## Wall-clock budget
| chains | total length @ 24fps | est. wall-clock |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~4 s | 20-25 min |
| 2 | ~8 s | 40-50 min |
| 3 | ~12 s | 60-75 min |
| 5 | ~20 s | 100-125 min |

Each chain replays the (LoRA + transformer) load cost cheaply since ComfyUI caches. Dominant cost is sampling — linear in num_chains.

## Caveats (intentional, deferred)
- **Visible junction seams** between segments. No overlap blending; LTX-2.3's \`LTXVAddGuide\` could fix this in a future PR.
- Sub-segments inherit the same prompt; no per-segment prompt steering yet.
- Memory unchanged (we never hold two segments in MPS at once).

## Test plan
- [x] 39/39 unit tests pass
- [ ] Manual: real chain-2 run end-to-end (will follow up in a comment)

author: hayes-mysten
body:
## Description

When a user calls `tx.setGasPrice(0)` to opt into the free-tier / address-balance gasless flow on a PTB whose only inputs are a `FundsWithdrawal` and pure args (e.g. `0x2::balance::send_funds<USDC>` for a recipient), `coreClientResolveTransactionPlugin`'s `setGasBudget` runs a simulate with `gasData.payment: []`. JSON-RPC's `dryRunTransactionBlock` then rejects the simulate with:

> Error checking transaction input objects: Invalid transaction expiration: Transactions must either have address-owned inputs, or a ValidDuring expiration with at most two epochs of validity

The gRPC server-side simulate fills in this expiration itself ([sui#26576](https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/26576)), but JSON-RPC's `dryRunTransactionBlock` does not. The existing resolver does set a `ValidDuring` later (after `setGasPayment` zeroes out the payment), but by then the simulate inside `setGasBudget` has already failed.

This change pre-fills the `ValidDuring` expiration before calling `setGasBudget` whenever `gasData.price === 0n`. The expiration would have been set anyway by the existing post-resolve check, so the wire bytes are unchanged — we just move the assignment earlier so the simulate can pass on JSON-RPC. `getCurrentSystemState` / `getChainIdentifier` are also added to the existing parallel fetch when gasless to avoid an extra round trip.

## Test plan

- Reproduced the bug end-to-end on testnet against `https://fullnode.testnet.sui.io:443`:
  - `tx.balance({ type: USDC, balance: 10_000n })` → `0x2::balance::send_funds<USDC>` → `tx.setGasPrice(0)`
  - Without the fix: `SuiJsonRpcClient.signAndExecuteTransaction` fails inside `setGasBudget`'s dryRun with the error quoted above.
  - With the fix: same tx succeeds. Confirmed digest `13QKGrXeHegj8ztHaFMsZdMDfVYE4RxE8qHucbAx4id7`.
- `pnpm --filter @mysten/sui exec tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `pnpm --filter @mysten/sui lint` passes.

author: nendy55555
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the Bet Analysis chat returned all-time NFL stats when asked about a specific year (e.g., "how profitable was I on NFL in 2024?"). Claude formatted the response with a "NFL 2024 Performance:" title even though the underlying data was unscoped, making wrong numbers look authoritative.

## What changed

**`js/parsers.js`** — `analyzeQuery` now detects a year token (`/\b(20\d{2})\b/`) and filters bets by `gameTime` year (falling back to `settledDate`/`addedDate`). The response label now includes the year (e.g., **NFL 2024**) so the scope is unambiguous.

**`js/chat.js`** —
- `buildBetContext(userMessage)` now parses the user's question for year + sport and builds a scope-specific view directly from `store.bets`, bypassing the dashboard `chartFilter` (which defaults to last 7 days). The context line now starts with `Scope: NFL 2024 | ...` so Claude knows exactly what slice it received.
- Context cache key now includes scope so different scoped questions don't collide.
- Dispatch: when the question has a year **and** the user has an API key, skip the local handler and route directly to Claude for a richer answer (~$0.002/query on Haiku 4.5).
- System prompt now forbids Claude from inventing stats for time periods/sports outside the Scope line.

## Why

The bet-tracker stores bets per-year (NFL 2024, NFL 2025, etc.) and the user's Excel sheets show year-by-year P/L. The previous chat flow had no year awareness anywhere — neither the local analyzer nor the Claude context — so 2024-specific questions silently returned all-time data dressed up with a "2024" title.

## Test plan

- [ ] Ask "how profitable was I on NFL in 2024?" — should show 2024-only stats, matching the user's spreadsheet (Andrew $617.49, Thomas $1,338.91, etc.)
- [ ] Ask "what's my NBA record in 2025?" — same year scoping for a different sport
- [ ] Ask "how am I doing on NFL?" (no year) — should still return current dashboard-filter scope, unaffected
- [ ] Ask about a year with no bets (e.g., "NFL 2019") — should return "No bets found"
- [ ] Verify cost stays under $0.005/query on Haiku 4.5

author: bradleygleaveportfolio
body:
## Summary

Finishes the half-built bulk invite + transactional email pipeline for the fitness launch. Mobile companion: PR #141.

### What's new
- **`EmailService` (`src/email/`)** — single transactional-email entry point. Transports: `resend` (production), `log` (dev/test). Doctrine: **no fake success.** When `EMAIL_TRANSPORT=resend` and `RESEND_API_KEY` / `EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` are missing, the app refuses to boot rather than silently dropping sends.
- **`EmailSendLog`** Prisma model with `idempotency_key UNIQUE`. Every `send()` requires a caller-supplied key (e.g. `invite:<invite_code_id>`); the second call with the same key is a no-op that returns `status: 'skipped'`. Support has a permanent ledger for "did we send X to Y on Z" investigations.
- **8 launch templates** (Handlebars) — `coach-invites-client`, `payment-reminder`, `payment-failed`, `coach-onboarding-welcome`, `client-onboarding-welcome`, `weekly-digest`, `payment-receipt`, `dunning-final`. Each carries its own subject line.
- **Bulk invite send** — `InviteCodesService.bulkInvite` now delivers one `coach-invites-client` email per row, idempotent by `invite_code_id`. Per-row `email_status` (`sent` | `failed` | `skipped` | `logged`) is returned so the mobile UI can show ✓/✗ next to each recipient (matches mobile PR #141 contract).
- **Per-row resend endpoint** — `POST /coach/invite-codes/:id/send` for the "resend" button next to a failed row. Same idempotency key, so accidental double-tap is a no-op.
- **Audit row** — `invite.bulk_sent` written once per bulk call with `total_requested / created_count / sent_count / failed_count / logged_count / rejected_count` in metadata. Append-only via existing `AuditService`.
- **DNS + operator docs** — README §Resend (transactional email) now lays out the full SPF / DKIM (3× CNAME) / DMARC record set for the sending domain, plus an operator runbook for the missing-config boot failure.

### Mobile contract (PR #141)
The mobile PR expects `POST /coach/invite-codes/bulk` to return:
```ts
{
  total: number;
  created: Array<{
    email: string;
    code: string;
    invite_code_id: string;
    email_status: 'sent' | 'failed' | 'skipped' | 'logged';
    email_error?: string;
  }>;
  rejected: Array<{ email: string; reason: string }>;
}
```
This backend now produces exactly that shape. `email_status: 'logged'` is the dev-mode value (corresponds to `EMAIL_TRANSPORT=log`); production deployments will only see `sent` / `failed` / `skipped`.

### Not in scope
- DigestService still owns its own `_sendViaResend` helpers from Phase 9. Migrating that surface to the new `EmailService` is a follow-up — the launch-critical path is invite sends.
- The `sendgrid` / `postmark` branches in DigestService are untouched; the new `EmailService` accepts `resend` or `log` only.

## Testing

- [x] Full Jest suite: **1650 passed, 16 skipped, 5 todo across 161 suites** (~94 s).
- [x] New unit tests (56) cover:
  - Transport selection at construction (`log` default, throws on `resend` without `RESEND_API_KEY` / `EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`, rejects unknown transport names)
  - Rendering for all 8 templates without throwing
  - Idempotency: P2002 on `EmailSendLog.idempotency_key` returns `status: 'skipped'` without re-hitting the transport
  - Failed Resend response (`422`) is recorded and surfaced as `status: 'failed'`, not swallowed
  - Invalid recipient returns `status: 'failed'` without writing a row
  - `bulkInvite` calls `EmailService.send` once per row with `idempotencyKey = 'invite:<id>'`
  - Per-row `email_status` propagates back to the caller (sent / failed)
  - `sendInviteEmailForCode` IDOR guard (rejects when row belongs to a different coach) + revoked-row guard
  - One `invite.bulk_sent` audit row per bulk call with correct per-status counts

## Pre-merge operator checklist

- [ ] Verify the sending domain (e.g. `send.thegrowthproject.app`) in the Resend dashboard
- [ ] Add SPF / DKIM / DMARC records per README §Resend
- [ ] `fly secrets set EMAIL_TRANSPORT=resend RESEND_API_KEY=re_... EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=team@send.thegrowthproject.app`
- [ ] Deploy + smoke a bulk invite of one recipient
- [ ] Confirm `EmailSendLog` row written and provider message id matches the Resend dashboard

author: potabk
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
Upstream PR [vllm-project/vllm#39568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39568) is a complete rewrite of the routed-experts capture/transport pipeline. It supersedes both:

- The original 0.20.2 design — `RoutedExpertsCapturer.get_instance()` singleton, `save_captured_experts(indices=...)`, shared-memory + `fcntl.flock` cross-process transport.
- The intermediate PR #39917 design — module-level `get_global_experts_capturer()`, `init_routed_experts_capturer_with_shared_cache()`, `issue_routing_d2h_copy()`, `extract_routed_experts_for_current_batch()`. This API existed in main for only a few days and was never in a stable release; it has been **fully removed**.

After the upgrade to vLLM 0515, vllm-ascend faces two API surfaces that are incompatible at the source level:

| Aspect | 0.20.2 | main |
|---|---|---|
| Capturer access | `RoutedExpertsCapturer.get_instance()` (singleton) | `runner.routed_experts_capturer` (per-runner instance, no global) |
| Per-step `clear_buffer` | via singleton | via runner attribute |
| Per-step D2H + ship | `capturer.save_captured_experts(indices=cpu_slot_mapping)` (sync, shm write) | runner-managed pinned `routed_experts_cpu` D2H + `RoutedExpertsLists` on `ModelRunnerOutput.routed_experts` |
| Output channel | shm/flock to scheduler | `ModelRunnerOutput.routed_experts: RoutedExpertsLists` (NamedTuple, msgpack + zmq IPC) |
| `slot_mapping` source | `slot_mapping.cpu().numpy()` saved to `self.cpu_slot_mapping` | private device snapshot `routed_experts_slot_mapping_device`, then pinned `routed_experts_slot_mapping_cpu` |
| Layer hook injection | `select_experts` calls singleton from inside `apply()` | `module.router.set_capture_fn(...)` from `_bind_routed_experts_capturer` |

## Strategy Overview

1. **Keep the 0.20.2 path intact.** It already works end-to-end. All 0.20.2-specific call sites stay byte-identical.
2. **Add a parallel main path** gated by `vllm_version_is("0.20.2") == False`. Reuse upstream `GPUModelRunner.init_routed_experts_capturer()` (inherited) for buffer allocation; override only `_bind_routed_experts_capturer` because Ascend's `select_experts` does not go through upstream `BaseRouter`.
3. **Async scheduling: piggyback on upstream `AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput`.** vllm-ascend already constructs that wrapper directly, so adding the `routed_experts=` kwarg is enough — the wrapper handles `to_cpu_nonblocking()` on its copy stream and `tolists()` finalization in `get_output()` for free.
4. **No new compat module, no monkey patches.** Branching is inline at each call site; total surface is one new method (`_bind_routed_experts_capturer`) plus three branched call sites in `model_runner_v1.py` and one in `fused_moe.py`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

### How was this patch tested?

- vLLM version: v0.20.2
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ce29c26b31d432b1b4bc028c46bb2c3b07a667d8

body:
## Summary
- `ssh/config` の `IdentityFile` が存在しない `~/.ssh/id_rsa` を指しており、SSH認証が `Permission denied (publickey)` で失敗していた
- 実際に存在しGitHubにも登録済みの `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` を指すよう修正
- 副次的に Claude Code のプラグインインストール時の SSH clone エラー（`SSH host key is not in your known_hosts file`）の根本原因となっていた状態を解消

## Background
- `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` は GitHub に `ed25519-auth-key-20260401` (auth) と `ed25519-signing-key-20260401` (signing) として登録済み
- `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -T git@github.com` は成功するが、configの IdentityFile が `id_rsa` 固定指定されていたため、デフォルトでは id_rsa を見にいって失敗していた
- ed25519 は GitHub・OpenSSH の現在の推奨アルゴリズム

## Test plan
- [x] `ssh -T git@github.com` が認証成功すること（`Hi lacolaco! You've successfully authenticated`）
- [ ] このPRのレビューチェックアウトが SSH 経由で問題なく動くこと

## Summary
Adds a manual-only live smoke harness for plan extraction providers. The script sends a small deterministic plan fixture to `/api/ai/plan-extract`, records only sanitized JSON, and can compare Free and Pro paths against a selected preview or production endpoint.

## Root cause
Production upload failures were hard to reproduce because provider tests were mostly mocked and there was no guarded live command that exercised the same API route without printing secrets or raw payloads.

## Changes
- Added `scripts/ai-plan-extract-smoke.mjs` with `--mode free-cloud|paid|both`, `--file`, `--fixture`, `--endpoint`, auth options, timeout, and JSON output.
- Required `AI_LIVE_PROVIDER_SMOKE=true` before any live request.
- Added deterministic PNG/JPG/PDF plan fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`.
- Added manual-only `AI provider smoke` workflow with `workflow_dispatch`, read-only permissions, and sanitized report artifact upload.
- Added `npm run ai:plan-extract:smoke`.
- Added tests for guard behavior, missing local provider config, sanitized reports, output files, and workflow safety.

## Validation
- `npm run test -- tests/ai-provider-smoke-script.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run test`
- `npm run build`

## Risk
Low. The workflow has no schedule and does not run on pull requests. The live script refuses to run unless explicitly guarded by `AI_LIVE_PROVIDER_SMOKE=true`, and report output omits provider raw payloads, base64, models, tokens, auth headers, and secrets.

Commit 3 is the rebase-induced delta: when commit 1 was originally created on 2026-05-14, A4a/A4b/A5/A6 were still local branches in review. The merged forms (with their own PR-merge artifacts and the CI-fix `6dea74bd` on the A6 branch) produced an additional +287/-50 lines of typed-class symbols in `ai-engine/SKELETON.md` once E was rebased onto the new `main`. Pure additions of typed BaseTool / Pydantic input classes; the 50 removed lines are pre-A6 standalone `@tool`-decorator function signatures that no longer exist at module scope.

## Files changed
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — `crew/` listing replaced with `services/`, `PortkitConversionCrew` → `ConversionPipeline`
- `CLAUDE.md` — datestamp + AI Engine stack refresh + PLUR Memory section now part of canonical constant

- Generator runs idempotently: re-running on the rebased tip produces zero diff against committed state

Commit 1 (the regen) and commit 2 (the script change) have semantically distinct intents — separating them keeps each diff narrow and makes either independently revertable.

Commit 1's message describes the local-branch state on 2026-05-14. The +287/-50 delta in commit 3 reflects a *different* working-tree snapshot (the rebased tip with the actual merged PRs, including the CI fix). ## Summary

Hardens the Free image upload path so oversized plan images are resized before provider calls, transient Gemini image failures get one bounded retry, and Free image provider failures return safer product-level reasons.

## Root cause

The Free path was forwarding raw image bytes directly to providers and treated all image provider-chain failures as one generic unavailable state. Large images and transient Gemini failures could fail without enough safe diagnostics to distinguish timeout, external rate limit, or provider unavailability.

## Changes

- Add server-side image preprocessing with `sharp` for PNG/JPEG/WebP uploads.
- Resize oversized images to a 2048px max dimension and convert heavy PNGs to JPEG when the processed output is useful.
- Add one retry for transient Gemini Free image failures; OpenRouter 429 is recorded as external rate limit and is not retried.
- Extend diagnostic records with image-processing metadata and provider-attempt metadata without raw files, base64, secrets, URLs, or stack traces.
- Return safe Free image failure reasons: `free-image-provider-unavailable`, `free-image-provider-rate-limited`, and `free-image-provider-timeout`.

## Validation

- `npm run test -- tests/ai-image-preprocess.test.ts tests/ai-providers.test.ts tests/ai-plan-extract-route.test.ts tests/ai-plan-extract-diagnostics.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run test`
- `npm run build`

## Risk

Low to medium. The change uses existing `sharp` dependency on the node runtime and does not change PDF handling, paid/OpenAI routing, pricing, Supabase, or billing. Free image uploads now do extra CPU work before provider calls for oversized images.

author: vivekchand
body:
Closes the alerts/rules outlier from PR #1258.

## Why

PR #1258 routed `/api/alerts/rules` (and `/api/channels/<provider>/status`) through `local_store_via_daemon`, but the corresponding methods weren't in `_DAEMON_METHODS`. Every call hit:

1. POST `/__local_query__/query_alert_rules` → 400 \"method not allowed\"
2. Helper returns None (treated as \"daemon unreachable\")
3. Single-process fallback: `get_store(read_only=True)` → IOException (sync daemon holds the OS-level file lock)
4. Caught → returns None  
5. Handler falls through to legacy gateway-RPC path → 6 s timeout

## Verified

Post-PR #1258 deploy on 0.12.196:

| Endpoint | Time |
|---|---|
| /api/crons | 180 ms ✓ |
| /api/autonomy | 6 ms ✓ |
| /api/component/brain | 5 ms ✓ |
| **/api/alerts/rules** | **5-7 s ✗** |

The 4th one was the outlier — exactly because of this allowlist gap.

## Fix

Add `query_alert_rules` + `query_channel_config_status` to `_DAEMON_METHODS`. Both already exist as LocalStore methods (`clawmetry/local_store.py:2685`).

3 / -0 lines.

## Test plan

author: eyalm321
body:
Fixes two **independent** crashes hitting `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on workspaces with `injectWorkspacePackages: true` (or `dependenciesMeta.*.injected`), surfaced via `turbo prune --docker` pipelines.

## Bug 1 — peer-variant snapshot missing `resolution` (lean, defense-in-depth)

A peer-variant injected workspace snapshot (`@scope/pkg@file:packages/pkg(peerA@1)(peerB@2)`) inherits its `resolution` from the base `packages:` entry (`@scope/pkg@file:packages/pkg`). When a tool prunes the lockfile and drops that base entry, readers that deref `pkgSnapshot.resolution` crash with the cryptic:

```
Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'directory' in undefined
```

**The root cause is upstream of pnpm**: the pruner (e.g. `turbo prune`) emits an internally inconsistent lockfile. Fixed at the source in **vercel/turborepo#12825** (retain the base entry for peer-variant injected deps; minimal repro in **vercel/turborepo#12824**) — empirically verified to produce a correct pruned lockfile for a real multi-service workspace.

**pnpm side (this PR): one lean normalization at the read layer** — in `convertToLockfileObject`, where base→variant inheritance already happens via `Object.assign`. When the base entry is absent, reconstruct the directory resolution from the `file:` depPath. This is *reconstruction, not guessing*: for a workspace `file:` dep the directory **is** the depPath suffix — exactly what pnpm's own writer emits. It is **defense-in-depth, not load-bearing**: with a well-formed lockfile (turbo#12825 or any correct input) the branch never fires. Because the normalization sits at the single shared read layer, it also covers the sibling `Cannot use 'in' operator … 'integrity' in undefined` on the `pnpm deploy` path (same `resolution === undefined` root, different deref site).

Per review feedback: the earlier per-reader `inheritOrSynthesizeResolution` helper across 5 call sites is **removed**; normalization lives in exactly one place (`convertToLockfileObject`), and the readers are back to `main`.

## Bug 2 — lifecycle re-import wipes `.bin/<tool>` (pure pnpm; the substantive fix)

`runLifecycleHooksConcurrently` re-imports an injected workspace package into its targets after `prepare`/`postinstall`. The 2022 `scanDir`-into-`filesMap` workaround (#4299) fed target-internal paths to `importPackage`; once #11088 made `importIndexedDir`'s `makeEmptyDir` fast path the default, that path wipes the target's `node_modules` before copying, so the re-import dies with `ERR_PNPM_ENOENT` on `node_modules/.bin/<tool>`.

Fix: drop the `scanDir` workaround and pass `keepModulesDir: true` so `importIndexedDir` skips the destructive fast path and preserves the target's existing `node_modules` (bin symlinks + transitive deps) via its staging/move path. Stays on `storeController.importPackage`, so source files keep their **hardlinks** (no copy-loop regression). Net reduction vs `main`: the `scanDir` helper and the `node:fs` / `FilesMap` imports are removed.

## Tests

- The `deps-restorer` regression fixture `peer-variant-missing-resolution` **omits the base `packages:` entry**, so it encodes the actual pruned shape and reproduces the crash on `main`: reverting the `convertToLockfileObject` change yields `resolution: undefined` for the peer-variant (→ the `lockfileToDepGraph` crash); with this PR it is reconstructed as `{ type: 'directory', directory: … }`.
- A `lockfile.fs` unit test pins the heuristic boundary: a directory resolution is synthesized for a pruned `file:` peer-variant but **never** for a `file:` tarball.
- A `deps-installer` regression test covers the Bug 2 re-import (injected dep with a `prepare` script + a bin-having dependency).

## Validation

End-to-end on a real `injectWorkspacePackages` monorepo (`turbo prune --docker` → `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`), on services that crash on **both** bugs with stock pnpm:

- pnpm with both fixes: the crashing services build.
- **vercel/turborepo#12825 + pnpm with only Bug 2** (Bug 1 fully reverted): the crashing services still **build** → confirms Bug 1 here is genuine defense-in-depth and turbo#12825 owns the root cause.
- Bug 2 reproduces on stock pnpm regardless of turbo (it is purely pnpm's importer fast-path).

Pairs with **vercel/turborepo#12825** (Bug 1 root cause; minimal repro **vercel/turborepo#12824**). Tracks #11663.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed crashes when `injectWorkspacePackages: true` is enabled with pruned lockfiles containing peer-dependency variants.
  * Resolved `node_modules/.bin` tool references being lost during lifecycle hook re-import, preventing `ENOENT` errors.

author: calithedog
body:
## Summary
Four features focused on the console-second-screen audience and on giving the project a path to discovery:

### 1. Wake Lock — fixes the #1 pain point of the second-screen pitch
Phones auto-lock after 30s, which makes "open it on your phone next to the TV" basically unusable. While any boss timer is running, the app requests a screen wake lock via `navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')` and releases it when all timers stop. A `visibilitychange` listener re-acquires when the tab returns to foreground (the API drops the lock automatically on tab hide).

Silent: no UI; just works on supporting browsers (Chrome 84+, Edge 84+, Safari 16.4+). Falls through harmlessly on unsupported browsers.

### 2. PWA / Add to Home Screen
- `manifest.json` with `name`, `short_name`, theme color, scope, icons
- `sw.js` service worker with app-shell caching (offline-friendly, network-falls-back-to-cache)
- `icon.svg` — gold "IC" monogram on a dark background, matches the in-app aesthetic
- HTML head additions: manifest link, theme-color meta, apple-touch-icon, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`, `viewport-fit=cover`
- Document title renamed to **ESO Imperial City Tracker** to match the README

Result: Android/Chrome users get the install banner; iOS users can "Add to Home Screen" and the app opens fullscreen without browser chrome.

### 3. OBS browser-source mode — `?obs=1`
Strips the header, theme buttons, mute button, help button, map, Tel Var panel, action strip, and reset button. Transparent background. Compact 380px-wide layout showing only **Next Respawn** + the **6 district timers**. Streamers can drop the URL straight into OBS as an overlay.

Also skips the help-modal auto-open in OBS mode (so streamers don't get the welcome dialog on every refresh).

### 4. Smarter Seen Alive
When `seenAlive(i)` is called while a kill timer with >30s remaining is still running, the log entry and toast now explicitly say "stale timer cleared" so the user knows their previous kill data was overridden. The under-30s path is unchanged (just normal "seen alive" messaging).

## Files changed
- `index.html` — head meta tags, OBS CSS block, wake-lock JS, seenAlive enhancement, OBS init guard, service-worker registration
- `js/app.js` — wake-lock JS, seenAlive enhancement, OBS init guard (kept in sync per CLAUDE.md)
- **New:** `manifest.json`, `sw.js`, `icon.svg`

## Test plan
- [x] 154/154 in-browser tests still pass
- [x] Manifest loads, service worker registers, icon reachable, title = "ESO Imperial City Tracker"
- [x] `wakeLock` functions exist and `'wakeLock' in navigator` is true
- [x] Seen Alive with 10-min running timer → toast: "Memorial seen alive — stale timer cleared"
- [x] Seen Alive with no timer → toast: "Memorial seen alive" (unchanged)
- [x] `/?obs=1` → body has `obs` class, header/mute/theme/help/map/telvar/action/reset all `display:none`, districts + next-up visible, transparent background, compact 380px width
- [x] Help modal does NOT auto-open in OBS mode
- [ ] Real-device sanity check on phone (install banner, wake lock holds during farming)
- [ ] OBS browser-source check: load `?obs=1` in OBS, confirm transparent backdrop renders correctly

## Notes for reviewer
- The SVG icon is intentionally simple — Android/Chrome accept SVG icons for the manifest. iOS Safari is more strict and will fall back to a screenshot for the home-screen icon. Adding PNG variants is a polish item for later.
- Service worker uses cache-first for same-origin GETs only. Google Fonts is cross-origin so it doesn't hit the SW cache (handled by the browser's HTTP cache instead).
- The wake lock is released automatically when the user closes the tab; no leak on page unload.

body:
## What
Adds the restaurant-light vertical module — a self-contained, opt-in CRM module for restaurant and catering clients, built in parallel with Phases 11–13.

## Why
Phase 14 depends only on Phases 1–10 (all shipped) and has zero dependency on Phase 11 (RAG/compliance), Phase 12 (salon/spa), or Phase 13 (mobile/service-hub). A paying restaurant/catering lead makes this the right time to implement it. The module composes existing Phase 6/7/9 infrastructure rather than introducing new cross-cutting concerns.

## Changes

**New module: `module/restaurantlight/`**
- `MenuItem` — menu catalog with course, dietary flags, modifiers, available toggle; collection `restaurant_light_menu_items`
- `CateringOrder` — inquiry → quote-sent → confirmed → completed lifecycle; `issueQuote()` creates a Phase-7 DRAFT `Quote` linked to the order's contact and annotates it with event details (headcount, date, dietary requirements, special requests)
- `Reservation` — lightweight PENDING → CONFIRMED → SEATED → COMPLETED / NO_SHOW / CANCELLED lifecycle for tastings and private events; `externalRef` holds Tock/OpenTable IDs for future webhook ingestion
- Three `TenantScopedReactiveMongoRepository` interfaces (`MenuItemRepository`, `CateringOrderRepository`, `ReservationRepository`)
- Three services (`MenuItemService`, `CateringOrderService`, `ReservationService`); all reactive, no `@Service` annotation — registered exclusively via `RestaurantLightAutoConfiguration`
- Three staff controllers (`MenuItemController`, `CateringOrderController`, `ReservationController`) with `@ConditionalOnProperty` gating and `TenantModuleRegistry.requireEnabled` per-handler guard
- `CateringOrderController` adds `POST /{id}/issue-quote`, `POST /{id}/confirm`, `POST /{id}/complete` transition endpoints
- `ReservationController` adds `POST /{id}/confirm`, `/{id}/seat`, `/{id}/complete`, `/{id}/no-show`, `/{id}/cancel` transition endpoints

**Public widget**
- `POST /public/widget/restaurant-reservation/{token}` — anonymous reservation submission; upserts contact by email + tenant (same pattern as Phase 10e service-request widget); creates `Reservation` in `PENDING` status; uses `ReservationRepository` directly (not the service) so it boots without requiring the tenant-level module gate

**Auto-configuration**
- `RestaurantLightAutoConfiguration` (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@ConditionalOnProperty(prefix = "kmosf.modules.restaurant-light", name = "enabled")`) registers service beans and `ModuleDefinition`

**Cross-cutting**
- `DomainEventType`: adds `CATERING_ORDER_QUOTE_ISSUED`, `CATERING_ORDER_CONFIRMED`, `RESERVATION_CREATED` constants for WorkflowRule automations
- `application.properties`: adds `kmosf.modules.restaurant-light.enabled=${KMOSF_MODULE_RESTAURANT_LIGHT:false}` (off by default)

## Test plan
- [ ] `./gradlew build -x test` — clean compile (Testcontainers/Docker unavailable in this environment; test failures are pre-existing)
- [ ] With `KMOSF_MODULE_RESTAURANT_LIGHT=true ./gradlew bootTestRun`: `POST /api/restaurant-light/menu-items` → 201; `POST /api/restaurant-light/catering-orders` → 201; `POST /{id}/issue-quote` → order transitions to QUOTE_SENT, Quote created in Phase-7 collection; `POST /api/restaurant-light/reservations` → 201; `POST /api/public/widget/restaurant-reservation/{token}` → contact upserted + reservation created → 200 with both IDs
- [ ] With module disabled (default): all `/restaurant-light/**` and `/public/widget/restaurant-reservation/**` routes return 404

body:
# Description

- Requires https://github.com/uselagoon/machinery/pull/127
- Resolves https://github.com/uselagoon/lagoon-cli/issues/233
- Could continue work to additionally resolve https://github.com/uselagoon/lagoon-cli/issues/262

This PR introduces support for adding `COMMAND`-type advanced task definitions to lagoon environments via the command 
```bash
lagoon add task-definition -p project -e main [-f filepath | -S service -c command -d description -C confirmation]
```

Simple definitions (i.e those with only a command, description, and confirmation text) can be done directly via cli arguments. Otherwise, if the user specifies a file path via the `-f` option, then the cli will read in a task definition defined in a YAML file. The file method is more full-featured, and supports most of the advanced task definition functionality available. For example:

```yaml
name: "example task"
description: "example task"
confirmationText: "Are you sure?"
service: cli
command: "echo $MY_VAR"
permission: DEVELOPER
deployTokenInjection: true
projectKeyInjection: true
adminOnlyView: false
arguments:
  - name: MY_VAR
    displayName: "My Variable"
    type: NUMERIC
    optional: false
    defaultValue: "1122"
``` 

# Limitations

- Doesn't yet support the `IMAGE` task definition type
- At this point in time, only supports defining a task definition on an environment (not project)

author: direwolfvm
body:
## Summary

Adds two self-serve mechanisms for users to reset a forgotten password — no email link required.

- **Recovery codes** — 8 single-use codes (`XXXXX-YYYYY`, 31-char alphabet) generated at `/settings/security`, shown exactly once, sha256-hashed at rest, consumed via `UPDATE…RETURNING` so the same code can't be used twice.
- **Authenticator app (TOTP, RFC 6238)** — hand-rolled HMAC-SHA1, 30s step, 6 digits, ±1 window. Setup shows a QR code (rendered server-side with `qrcode`) + base32 secret. The secret stores as BYTEA but `totp_enabled` lags it: an abandoned scan can't lock the user out.
- **`POST /api/auth/reset`** — `{email, mechanism: 'recovery'|'totp', proof, newPassword}` → bcrypt-rehashes password on success. Always returns the same generic `invalid email or proof` error on failure so the endpoint can't be used to enumerate accounts.
- **`/forgot`** page with form + linked from `/login` ("Forgot your password? Reset it").
- **Migration 0007** — adds `users.totp_secret BYTEA`, `users.totp_enabled BOOLEAN`, and `recovery_codes` table with `(user_id, code_hash)` unique index plus a partial index on `(user_id) WHERE used_at IS NULL` for the consumption query.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] Migration 0007 applies clean on a fresh DB
- [x] 17-step end-to-end script: signup → generate 8 codes → bogus code rejected (generic msg) → wrong email rejected (generic msg) → valid code resets password & returns `remaining: 7` → reused code rejected → login with new password works → TOTP setup → bogus code rejected → correct code enables → TOTP-based reset works → disable → TOTP-based reset now rejected → `DELETE` invalidates all codes
- [x] `/forgot` and `/login` HTML render with new links

body:
## Summary
- Tightens the two-step `prepare_report_delivery` → `deliver_report` flow so the confirmation token is bound to the **prepared** OCI Notifications topic, not just to the fact that *some* prepare happened.
- Without this, a caller could prepare delivery for topic A, get a token, then call `deliver_report` with topic B and the same token — sending the email to a recipient the user never confirmed. New error code `email_delivery_recipient_mismatch` blocks that path and instructs the caller to re-prepare.
- `_recipients_from_delivery_state` is rewritten so the prepared topic is the source of truth (instead of "first non-empty wins"), and the `get_report_delivery_options` workflow guidance now points callers at `prepare_report_delivery` + `delivery_confirmation_token`.
- README and the `reports-and-playbooks` spec are updated to show the new prepare → confirm → deliver sequence in all examples.

## Test plan
- [x] New regression test `test_deliver_report_rejects_changed_email_topic_after_prepare` exercises the bypass scenario and asserts `report_delivery_service.deliver` is not awaited.
- [x] Existing `TestDeliverReportHandler` suite still passes.
- [ ] Manual: run `prepare_report_delivery` → `deliver_report` with matching topic → expect `sent`; repeat with a changed `email_topic_ocid` → expect `email_delivery_recipient_mismatch`.

body:
## Summary

- Adds 12 denormalized fields from the parent survey onto each `survey_response` indexer payload (`survey_title`, `survey_status`, `survey_cutoff_date`, `is_nps_survey`, `is_project_survey`, `committee_name`, `committee_category`, `creator_name`, `survey_created_at`, `survey_last_modified_at`, `total_responses`, `total_recipients`)
- Opens the `v1-objects` KV bucket in `EventProcessor` and threads the handle through the KV handler chain to `handleSurveyResponseUpdate`
- Fetches the parent survey (after both mapping checks pass) and calls `convertMapToSurveyData` to extract fields; matches committee name by v1 committee ID with fallback to first committee
- Updates `docs/indexer-contract.md` to document the new fields and explain why denormalization is needed

## Context

Survey takers do not hold the `survey:{uid}:viewer` relation and cannot resolve survey details through the query service. The `lfx-self-serve` "My Surveys" page was working around this by calling `GET /surveys/{uid}` for each response, which fails with a 403 for respondents and falls back to a useless stub row. Denormalizing these fields at index time eliminates the N+1 fetch entirely.

A follow-up ticket (LFXV2-1843) tracks re-indexing all survey responses when the parent survey is updated, so denormalized fields stay in sync after title/status changes.

body:
## Summary
Tightens `firestore.rules` for `/configCurrent/{document=**}`: read access removed (was `allow read: if true`).

## Why
Pre-change, any anonymous internet caller could hit Firestore REST and lift:
- `remoteButtonPushKey` (one half of door-control auth — the X-RemoteButtonPushKey header)
- All four email allowlists (`remoteButtonAuthorizedEmails`, `featureSnoozeAllowedEmails` if present, `featureFunctionListAllowedEmails`, `featureDeveloperAllowedEmails`)
- The device `buildTimestamp` (FCM topic seed + httpEcho event-forgery seed)

Reproduction (currently works on prod, will 403 after this PR deploys):
\`\`\`
curl 'https://firestore.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/databases/(default)/documents/configCurrent/current'
\`\`\`

Security audit reference: finding C3 (configCurrent publicly readable).

## Why this is safe
Android + ESP32 do NOT read Firestore directly — they reach config through the `httpServerConfig` Cloud Function (gated by the static `X-ServerConfigKey` header). Cloud Functions use the Admin SDK and bypass client-side rules. Firebase Console reads also use Admin SDK and are unaffected.

This is a defense-in-depth fix. The static `X-ServerConfigKey` exposure (audit finding C5) is a separate, larger architectural issue not covered by this PR.

## Out of scope
- `eventsCurrent` and `updateAll` remain `allow read: if true`. Door state is meant to be observable. Tightening those is a separate decision.

## Test plan
- [x] Diff inspection: single rule changed
- [ ] First deploy will require `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` (or whatever the user's deploy flow is) — these rules don't auto-deploy on every PR merge

author: jamesbrink
body:
## Summary

Introduces a per-user runtime directory at `~/.ptywright/` plus a `tracing`-based structured-logging stack so ptywright behaves predictably as a long-running local daemon. The dotdir mirrors sibling utensils projects (`~/.mold`) and deliberately avoids XDG split locations on macOS — everything ptywright owns lives under one root that is easy to inspect, back up, and remove.

## Motivation

ptywright was reaching the point where ad-hoc `eprintln!` diagnostics weren't enough:

- `serve --stdio` reserves stdout for JSON-RPC, so stderr was the *only* diagnostic channel and there was no on-disk audit trail of past activity.
- `run` bridges raw bytes to the user's terminal — any extra stderr would corrupt the live PTY session, leaving us with effectively no observability at all in that mode.
- Configuration had nowhere to live, so every behavior change required a code edit or an env var.
- Sensitive-looking content in diagnostics was redacted at some callsites and not others.

This change establishes a single home for config and logs, picks the right sink combination per CLI mode automatically, and runs every record through ptywright's existing `RedactionPolicy` so secrets never reach disk or stderr through ptywright-owned events.

## What changed

### New modules

- **`src/paths.rs`** — `Paths::from_env()` resolves `PTYWRIGHT_HOME` → `~/.ptywright/` → `./.ptywright` (only if `HOME` is unset). Per-layout accessors (`home`, `config_path`, `logs_dir`, `data_dir`, `transcripts_dir`, `sockets_dir`), lazy `ensure_dir`, and an `expand_tilde` helper for paths that come from config strings.
- **`src/config.rs`** — `Config` and `LoggingConfig` loaded from `~/.ptywright/config.toml`. Missing files, missing sections, and missing keys all fall back to documented defaults; unknown keys are tolerated for forward compatibility. New `Error::Config` variant.
- **`src/logging.rs`** — Mode-specific `tracing` init that upholds each subcommand's output contract:

| Mode                       | Stderr | File | Notes                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | :----: | :--: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init_for_run`             |   ✗    |  ✓   | `run` owns the user's terminal — extra stderr would corrupt the PTY.   |
| `init_for_serve_stdio`     |   ✓    |  ✓   | stdout is JSON-RPC framing only and is never written.                  |
| `init_for_serve_socket`    |   ✓    |  ✓   | Same as `--stdio`.                                                     |
| `init_for_oneshot`         |   ✓    |  ✗   | Minimal init for `--help`, `--version`, `completions`.                 |

Daily rotation via `tracing-appender`, configurable retention (`max_days = 0` disables the sweep), `PTYWRIGHT_LOG` env override, and a `RedactingMakeWriter` adapter that runs every record through the existing `RedactionPolicy` before any sink sees the bytes.

### CLI wiring

- `main.rs` picks the right `init_*` per subcommand and holds the `LogGuard` for the lifetime of the process so the non-blocking writer can flush at exit.
- The "listening on socket/pipe" notice and socket client errors are now structured `tracing::info!` / `tracing::warn!` events carrying a `socket=` field, so the same record lands in stderr and the rotated log file with consistent formatting and redaction.
- CLI help for `serve --socket` no longer claims Windows is unsupported; the `interprocess`-backed named-pipe path has been live for a while and the help text was simply stale.

### Documentation

- New **`website/guide/runtime-directory.md`** describing the layout, env vars (`PTYWRIGHT_HOME`, `PTYWRIGHT_LOG`), config schema, log rotation/retention, redaction, and the per-mode sink selection table. Wired into the VitePress sidebar under "Design".
- `README.md` gains a "Runtime directory and logging" section.
- `AGENTS.md` architecture lists `paths.rs`, `config.rs`, `logging.rs` and the invariant "never log to stdout in `serve --stdio` mode".
- `reference/cli.md`, `reference/library.md`, `reference/index.md`, and `reference/roadmap.md` document the new public API and runtime behavior.
- `guide/index.md` status section refreshed (the old "ptywright is a skeleton" copy was very out of date); `guide/quickstart.md` points at the new runtime-directory page.
- `config.example.toml` at the repo root mirrors `mold/config.example.toml` style.

### Dependencies

- `dirs` — cross-platform `home_dir()` resolution
- `toml` — config parsing
- `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` (`env-filter`, `fmt`, `json`), `tracing-appender` — logging stack

## Cross-cutting concerns

The cleanest pattern that fell out of this work was wrapping `tracing-subscriber`'s `MakeWriter` trait with a `RedactingMakeWriter<M>` adapter — every formatted record passes through `RedactionPolicy` exactly once, regardless of which sink (file or stderr) ultimately receives it. No callsite needs to remember to redact, and structured fields (`socket=/path/to/sock`) get the same treatment as message text.

The other invariant worth calling out is that **stdio mode's stdout-purity contract is enforced by the type/function name**, not by convention: `init_for_serve_stdio` deliberately never installs a stdout layer, so a future contributor cannot accidentally regress this by reaching for `tracing_subscriber::fmt()` directly. The existing `serve_stdio_returns_json_rpc_response` integration test would catch any regression anyway.

## Test plan

All checks green locally on macOS aarch64:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --locked` — **117 / 117 passing** (lib 92, bin 10, integration 15)
  - `paths::tests` — 7 new (resolution order, env override, `ensure_dir` idempotency, tilde expansion)
  - `config::tests` — 7 new (defaults, partial merge, malformed → typed error, forward-compat unknown keys, JSON format, file round-trip)
  - `logging::tests` — 8 new (retention sweeps, `max_days = 0` no-op, missing dir tolerated, `RedactingWriter` redacts secrets, `make_filter` env override + config + default fallback)
  - `cli_tests::run_writes_log_file_under_ptywright_home` — end-to-end integration test that `PTYWRIGHT_HOME` redirect creates `logs/ptywright.YYYY-MM-DD.log`
- [x] `cargo build --locked --release`
- [x] `cd website && bun run build` — VitePress builds clean

Smoke checks against the release binary (all with `PTYWRIGHT_HOME=$(mktemp -d)` so nothing landed in `~/.ptywright/`):

- [x] `--version`, `--help` print expected output
- [x] `run -- /bin/sh -lc 'printf smoke-ready'` produces `smoke-ready` and creates `$PTYWRIGHT_HOME/logs/ptywright.2026-05-15.log`
- [x] `serve --stdio` round-trip with `server.capabilities`: stdout is exactly one valid JSON-RPC response with **0 bytes** of log noise; stderr clean; log file present
- [x] `serve --socket` writes the structured `INFO ptywright: ptywright: listening on local socket socket=/tmp/...sock` event to **both** stderr and the log file
- [x] Retention sweep: a backdated `ptywright.2020-01-01.log` was deleted on the next init while `unrelated.txt` was preserved — confirms the prefix guard

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Confirm `serve --stdio` stdout remains protocol-only after this change
- [ ] Confirm log paths under `~/.ptywright/logs/` (or `$PTYWRIGHT_HOME/logs/`) match the documented `ptywright.YYYY-MM-DD.log` shape
- [ ] Confirm no `eprintln!` of secret-shaped content slipped through outside of `cli_error_message` (which still runs through `RedactionPolicy`)
- [ ] Optional: try `PTYWRIGHT_LOG="info,ptywright::rpc=debug" ptywright serve --stdio` to verify the env override path
